subject: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)
related_links: Linear: ENG-4821 (Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

Hi all — before the Hosted overload protection rollout expands beyond canary, I want to lock down how we want Dedicated to behave (and how we describe it) so we don’t surprise Dedicated customers.

A few things I’m trying to align on:

1) When a Dedicated pool is saturated (GPU queue depth / scheduler pressure), what do we return?
   - Is it still the same Redwood overload taxonomy (429/503 + Retry-After + Redwood error codes) as Hosted?
   - Or do we treat Dedicated differently (e.g., prefer 503 “temporarily unavailable” vs 429 “rate limited”) because they’re paying for capacity not a shared tier?

2) Shedding behavior
   - Dedicated customers expect “predictable throughput” more than “best effort.”
   - If we shed, we should be deterministic and clear: which reasons are valid for Dedicated (capacity_exhausted vs memory_pressure vs routing_unavailable)?

3) Autoscaling expectations
   - For Dedicated with autoscaling enabled: do we promise that shed events are transient and scale-up is the primary recovery path?
   - Any constraints we need in docs around scale-up latency (minutes) and recommended client retry/backoff?

4) SLA / comms
   - We need one clear sentence for Dedicated contracts / docs on what is and isn’t an SLA breach when shedding is active.

If you can reply with your preferred behavior + wording constraints, I’ll roll it into ENG-4837 and the Dedicated section of the docs update.

Thanks,
Lauren
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

+1 to aligning now.

SRE POV:
- We should use the same error taxonomy + shape everywhere (per ADR-0147) to avoid SDK/client inconsistency. That’s the whole point of “clear + customer-actionable errors.”
- BUT the HTTP mapping can differ slightly by product *as long as the error code + guidance is consistent*.

For Dedicated specifically:
- I strongly prefer 503 for “pool saturated / no immediate capacity” rather than 429, because 429 reads like “you violated a quota.” In Dedicated, it’s more like “capacity temporarily unavailable.”
- Include Retry-After always. It’s the best guardrail against retry storms.
- We should still cap queue depth and shed early; otherwise we’ll tail-latency collapse and then *everything* looks like an SLA breach.

Valid shed reasons for Dedicated (suggested):
- CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED (primary)
- MEMORY_PRESSURE (KV cache / OOM prevention) — but this should be rare and treated as a config/tuning signal
- CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE / ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE (if the routing service is degraded) — these should be noisy internally even if customer sees a clean 503

On autoscaling language: we should not promise recovery in X seconds. We can say “autoscaling may increase capacity; clients should honor Retry-After and use exponential backoff w/ jitter.”

Happy to review a proposed one-liner for SLA language once you draft.

Rafael
SRE Manager, Reliability

---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 11:21 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

Agree with Rafael on keeping one taxonomy.

Product/UX angle:
- Customers don’t care if it’s Hosted vs Dedicated — they care that they can programmatically handle it. So: same error code names, same JSON shape, same headers.
- For Dedicated, I also lean 503 over 429 for “pool saturated.”

One nuance: Some Dedicated customers have their own upstream rate limiting and will treat 429 differently (auto-throttle) vs 503 (retry aggressively). So if we do 503, the Retry-After guidance needs to be very explicit (and non-zero).

Another nuance: Dedicated “burst” / overflow.
- If a Dedicated customer has explicitly enabled overflow to Hosted / shared capacity (I know it’s rare), *that* should be a separate reason code so they can see it happened.

Draft wording suggestion (non-contract):
“During brief capacity saturation, Redwood may return 503 with a Retry-After header rather than queueing requests indefinitely; this behavior protects latency and service availability.”

Nikhil
PM — Hosted API

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 12:06 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

Decision / direction so we can move:

1) One taxonomy, one schema, one SDK behavior across products. Do not fork payload shape.
2) Dedicated default mapping for “pool saturated” = 503 + Retry-After + Redwood overload error code (not 429).
3) Dedicated should still shed deterministically to protect tail latency. The promise we make is “predictable behavior,” not “infinite queue.”

On SLA language: do not phrase shedding as “degraded mode” that implies we’re failing. Phrase it as overload protection / admission control.

Action items:
- Lauren: propose the Dedicated section language (docs + contract-friendly variant) and send for review by EOD.
- Rafael/Mina: make sure routing/gateway implementation can express this mapping cleanly (no surprise 429s on Dedicated unless it’s an explicit quota condition).
- Henry: sanity-check the customer-facing phrasing against the PRD requirements.

Sean
Director, SRE
Redwood Inference

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 2:09 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

Thanks — summarizing what I’m hearing as “locked” for Dedicated:

Behavior
- Same Redwood overload error schema + codes as Hosted (ADR-0147), surfaced consistently via SDKs.
- Default for Dedicated pool saturation: HTTP 503 + Retry-After.
- 429 only for true quota / policy violations (not capacity saturation).

Reasons (customer-visible)
- capacity_exhausted (expected under burst)
- memory_pressure (rare; indicates tuning needed)
- routing_unavailable / control_plane_unavailable (should page internally; customer sees clean 503)
- optional: dedicated_overflow_to_hosted (only if customer enabled overflow)

Docs wording draft (non-contract)
“Dedicated endpoints use overload protection to maintain predictable latency and availability. If the Dedicated pool is temporarily saturated, Redwood may reject requests with a 503 Service Unavailable response that includes a Retry-After header and a Redwood-specific overload error code. Clients should honor Retry-After and retry using exponential backoff with jitter.”

Contract/SLA-friendly one-liner draft
“Redwood may apply admission control during temporary capacity saturation to protect service stability; affected requests will receive a documented 503 response with Retry-After and do not indicate an internal service failure.”

Questions for Mina/Rafael:
- Can we guarantee that Dedicated pool saturation cannot accidentally fall through to “generic upstream 502/503” from the gateway? (I want the Redwood error code always.)

Henry — can you reply with any edits needed for tone/commitments?

I’ll update ENG-4837 with the above and link this thread.

Lauren

---

From: Henry Cho <henry_cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 3:47 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated alignment: overload / load-shedding behavior + SLA language (before Hosted rollout expands)

Edits to keep us safe:

- In the docs paragraph, I’d avoid “reject requests” (sounds punitive). Suggest “return an overload response” or “respond with 503…”.
- In the contract one-liner, I’d avoid “do not indicate an internal service failure” as an absolute. We can say “is intended to distinguish capacity saturation from internal errors” (so legal doesn’t interpret it as a guarantee).

Reword suggestion (contract-friendly):
“Redwood may apply admission control during temporary capacity saturation to protect service stability. In these cases, Redwood returns a documented 503 response with Retry-After and Redwood overload error codes to distinguish capacity saturation from internal errors.”

Otherwise looks good + aligned with the PRD direction.

Henry
PM — Customer-facing API behavior
Redwood Inference
